comment:
Cross-runtime behavior vectors for the retry/timeout mechanics behind an HTTP entry operation. `op` names an operation in spec.tono (retrying, retrying_with_timeout, or timeout_only); the TypeScript harness (runtimes/http-ts/test/parity.test.ts) compiles that spec, generates the real SDK, and drives it directly. Go and Rust are not repointed yet: their harnesses still run against the hand-written runtime package, using a small local op-name -> synthetic WireDescriptor lookup fed by `config` in place of the retired `descriptor` field. Each runtime runs every vector with random pinned to 0.5 and an instant, recording sleep. Script entries are consumed one per attempt: response returns that status/body, transport_failure fails the attempt, hang blocks until the per-attempt timeout fires. expect.attempts is the number of transport calls; expect.delays_ms are the backoff sleeps between attempts (random * min(2000, 100 * 2^retry)). `config` (max_retries / timeout_ms) is real client construction for the TypeScript harness and literal descriptor values for Go/Rust; no vector needs a late-bound ref anymore (see the removals below). A vector's optional declared_errors ([status, code|null, retryable] triples) stands in for spec.tono's own @errorCode/@retryable declarations: Go and Rust still build a retryable(status, body) predicate from it directly; the generated TypeScript SDK decides retryability for real, from the operation's own decode<Op>Error. A vector with no declared_errors means no error response is ever retryable.

Four vectors that existed before the generated SDK became the target are gone, not merely trimmed: (1) "the retry maximum resolves through a ref into the client values" and (2) "a ref that resolves to nothing disables retry" described a synthetic descriptor's `{ref: ...}` late binding, a concept the generated client has no equivalent of (a @retry field is always a real, always-resolved client field); (3) "a fractional retry maximum floors" is now a compile error, since @retry only accepts an integer-scalar field; (4) "an unresolved endpoint falls back to the caller base url" tested a fallback branch that PR #87 deleted outright after confirming it was unreachable (an entry @http operation always has a resolved endpoint field; there was never a public way to leave it unresolved). The fifth former vector, "the endpoint ref and declared headers resolve from the client values", survives as a `test` block in spec.tono instead of an entry here: it needs no timing seam, and the declarative form now generates the same assertion natively in all three languages.

vectors.name: no retry declared means one attempt, ever
a declared non-retryable error does not retry
an undeclared error status does not retry
the code discriminator blocks retry when the non-retryable error matches
the code discriminator allows retry when the retryable error matches
a null declared code matches any body, even one lacking a code field
a declared code with a non-matching body does not retry
exhausted retries return the last outcome
a timed-out attempt is a transport failure and retries
a timeout without retry surfaces as a transport outcome
